policy: Original authored factual paraphrases; no source document text or copied supplier prose. Synthetic wording, real attributed metadata.

passages.text: FVD specifies a 47.5 mm compressor inlet for its K16/24 conversion and describes changes to the housing contour, backplate and thrust bearing. The exact donor identity, complete wheel dimensions and compressor/turbine maps were not established by this product page.

questions.prompt: Does this FVD listing provide enough geometry to reproduce its turbo?
questions.answer: No. The 47.5 mm inlet is one dimension; the complete wheel profile, remaining dimensions, clearances, exact donor and performance maps are missing.

passages.text: The FVD page states a balancing process reaching 100,000 rpm. This describes a manufacturing test condition. It does not specify the maximum continuous operating speed of the 993 turbo.

questions.prompt: Can I use 100,000 rpm as the operating speed limit?
questions.answer: No. It is a stated balancing condition. A separate rotor operating envelope and speed limit are required.

passages.text: FVD advertises 555 hp when its turbo upgrade is combined with its software, intercoolers and supporting components. The page does not supply a measured 993 operating-point set, compressor map or turbine map. The unit hp is retained as published.

questions.prompt: Is 555 hp proven output from changing the turbos alone?
questions.answer: No. It is a supplier claim for a package including software, intercoolers and other components. No map or complete measured operating data were published on the consulted page.

passages.text: TTH offers a conversion using supplied original Porsche/BorgWarner K16 cores with size-8 hot housings. It advertises up to 650 PS with appropriate engine components and recalibration. It provides no measured map, operating speed envelope or test configuration on the consulted page.

questions.prompt: Does the TTH option match reuse of original K16s above 550 PS?
questions.answer: It is a documented candidate: it uses supplied K16 cores and advertises 650 PS with supporting changes. That capacity remains a supplier claim, requiring operating and engine validation.

questions.prompt: What power unit should be stored for this claim?
questions.answer: 650 PS, retaining the source unit rather than silently relabeling it bhp or wheel horsepower.

passages.text: TTH reports a balance figure of 0.05 g. The page does not identify the associated radius, residual-unbalance unit such as g mm, speed-dependent acceptance limits or balance grade.

questions.prompt: Does 0.05 g demonstrate rotor qualification?
questions.answer: No. Mass alone does not define residual unbalance without a radius, and the page lacks the acceptance conditions. Obtain the actual balance report and rotor operating limits.

passages.text: The TTH 750 PS product is based on K24 donors with size-10 hot housings. It is a different donor route from the K16-650 product, and its advertised power depends on engine components and software changes.

questions.prompt: Can the TTH 750 PS listing be recorded as a K16 conversion?
questions.answer: No. Its documented donor is K24 with size-10 hot housings. Keep it separate from the K16 option and retain the supporting-change condition.

passages.text: TTE describes the 993 TTE650 5050 as an upgrade of the original K16/8 pair. It specifies a 50 mm compressor inlet with 6+6 blades and a 50 mm turbine outlet, retaining the original K16 turbine with blade clipping. These dimensions are supplier data, not complete manufacturing geometry.

questions.prompt: Which original turbo elements are documented as retained?
questions.answer: The K16/8 hot housings and original K16 turbines are retained, with turbine clipping. The compressor and other components are modified; two wheel diameters do not define a reproducible design.

questions.prompt: Does this listing contain the hybrid compressor and turbine maps?
questions.answer: No. The consulted 993 product page does not provide those maps or a complete measured operating envelope.

passages.text: TTE advertises 650 PS for its 993 TTE650. The consulted listing contains no complete engine configuration, measured 993 dyno curve, compressor map or turbine map. A linked media archive is named for a 996 product and cannot establish a 993 result.

questions.prompt: Can the 996 media archive validate this 993 upgrade?
questions.answer: No. A 996 archive is evidence for a different application unless exact compatibility and test configuration are established. The 650 PS figure remains a supplier capacity claim.

passages.text: The TTE750 conversion requires K24 turbochargers and explicitly excludes K16 donors. Its page specifies a 51 mm compressor inlet, a 54 mm turbine outlet and K24/10 hot housings.

questions.prompt: Can I send my original K16 pair for the TTE750 conversion?
questions.answer: The published TTE750 donor requirement excludes K16 cores. It requires K24 turbochargers; it is not the same upgrade path as the K16-based TTE650.

passages.text: The TTE800 uses K24/10 hot housings and a replacement nine-blade turbine/shaft, with a 51 mm compressor inlet and 54 mm turbine outlet. Its more-than-800 PS claim is stated for 102 RON fuel and requires software changes. Maps and a complete operating envelope were not published.

questions.prompt: Is the TTE800 claim applicable to a stock K16 engine on unspecified fuel?
questions.answer: No. It concerns a K24-based conversion and explicitly states 102 RON fuel and recalibration. It does not establish stock K16 capacity or durability.

passages.application: TTE general VSR process versus 993 product
passages.text: TTE describes VSR balancing equipment that can reach 250,000 rpm for some applications. This general process statement is not a 250,000 rpm continuous operating limit for the 993 TTE650.

questions.prompt: What does the 250,000 rpm statement establish for this 993 turbo?
questions.answer: It describes equipment or process capability, dependent on application. It does not establish the turbo operating speed or its certified maximum.

passages.application: BorgWarner 993 stock and upgrade application table
passages.text: BorgWarner lists K16-6735 and K16-6736 for the 993 and prints a stock-turbo limit of 500 hp. The same application table lists upgrade references 5324 988 7003 and 5324 988 7004 with a 555 hp limit. These are catalogue capacity figures, not measured engine curves or compressor/turbine maps.

questions.prompt: Does the catalogue table reconstruct the stock K16 map?
questions.answer: No. It identifies the application and commercial capacity figures, but lacks pressure-ratio, corrected-flow, efficiency and shaft-speed fields. Preserve hp as printed.

passages.text: The BorgWarner 993 upgrade row prints maximum T3 values of 950 degrees C continuously and 980 degrees C temporarily. These values belong to the upgrade table. They do not establish measured stock-K16 exhaust temperature, alloy identity or a safe engine operating target.

questions.prompt: May I label 950 degrees C as the measured stock K16 exhaust temperature?
questions.answer: No. It is an upgrade-table temperature value, not a stock operating measurement or a complete engine thermal qualification.

passages.text: Cargraphic lists 475 PS at 6090 rpm and 632 Nm at 4550 rpm for a package containing modified K16/24 turbos and supporting changes to software, exhaust, intake and oil cooling. The consulted page does not publish the plotted test trace, boost trace or turbo maps.

questions.prompt: What kind of evidence is the Cargraphic data?
questions.answer: Nominal package power and torque points claimed by the tuner. They are useful comparisons for that configuration but are not compressor or turbine maps.

passages.text: The consulted Turbo Dynamics MD433 page did not establish a 993 donor, wheel geometry, power capacity or compressor/turbine map. A product title alone is insufficient to assert compatibility.

questions.prompt: Can MD433 be entered as a verified 993 hybrid?
questions.answer: No. The current evidence is a supplier lead without a verified 993 specification. Compatibility and performance remain unresolved.

passages.text: Turbo Technics describes performance and bespoke turbo work. No specific 993 product datasheet or exact 993 map was established from the generic page consulted.

questions.prompt: Does this generic supplier page prove a particular 993 conversion exists?
questions.answer: No. General manufacturing capability is not a specific product specification, donor identification or performance map.

passages.application: Current RUF UK Turbo R rebuild specification
passages.text: The current RUF UK Turbo R page pairs 405 kW with 550 bhp at 5500 rpm and lists 700 Nm at 4800 rpm. The power units disagree: 405 kW is approximately 550.6 PS or 543.1 mechanical hp. Preserve the printed values and flag the inconsistency instead of silently changing the label.

questions.prompt: How should the RUF power be normalized?
questions.answer: Store the printed pair with a unit-conflict flag. A computed conversion of 405 kW is about 550.6 PS or 543.1 mechanical hp; it cannot justify relabeling the source as internally consistent.

passages.application: Current and historical RUF Turbo R descriptions
passages.text: RUF UK describes a current Turbo R rebuild with its own ignition and engine-management specification. Rstrada lists a historical Turbo R description at 490 hp and 479 lb-ft without the associated rpm on that page. These entries describe different source contexts and should not be merged into one original factory specification.

questions.prompt: Can the current rebuild specification be assigned to every original Turbo R?
questions.answer: No. Keep current rebuild and historical descriptions separate. The available data do not establish that every original car used the current specification.

passages.text: Rstrada describes 3.6 litre CTR2 and CTR2 Sport engines with different power and torque ratings and charge-air cooling arrangements from a stock 993 Turbo. It does not identify the complete turbo reference or publish compressor/turbine maps.

questions.prompt: Does a related 3.6 litre air-cooled architecture establish stock K16 equivalence?
questions.answer: No. The engine configuration, intercoolers and turbo identity must be established separately. Related architecture alone cannot identify the stock 993 maps.

passages.application: Reported RUF Turbo R chassis-dyno result
passages.text: A Rennlist owner post describes a RUF Turbo R dyno result. An engine or chassis-dyno power curve plots engine output against engine speed. Without turbo inlet/outlet conditions, corrected flow and shaft speed, it cannot uniquely reconstruct a compressor/turbine map.

questions.prompt: Can this owner dyno result uniquely identify the turbo map?
questions.answer: No. It is an application result, not a turbo map. Many combinations of turbo, engine efficiency, temperatures and control settings can produce similar output.

passages.text: A forum transcription associates 468 lb-ft with 5500 rpm and separately reports 506 hp near that engine speed. Mechanical horsepower from those torque and rpm values is 468 times 5500 divided by approximately 5252, about 490 hp. The mismatch requires the original test sheet and unit conventions; it must not be silently corrected into a verified dyno curve.

questions.prompt: Do the reported 468 lb-ft, 5500 rpm and 506 hp form a consistent point?
questions.answer: No. The torque and speed imply about 490 mechanical hp. Flag the inconsistent transcription and obtain the original sheet instead of treating either number as a verified map.

passages.application: SJM KKK 2467 GGA/GGB map, Audi upgrade K16-6717
passages.text: SJM hosts a compressor-map scan for KKK 2467 GGA/GGB associated with turbo 5316 988 6717. The compressor family designation resembles that listed for the 993 K16, but the complete turbo reference and housing equivalence have not been established. It is a comparison lead rather than a validated 993 K16-6735/6736 map.

questions.prompt: Can this scan be labeled as the exact factory 993 K16 map?
questions.answer: No. The documented complete reference is 6717, not 6735 or 6736. Matching a compressor family name does not establish identical housings and tested configuration.

passages.text: The inspected SJM scan includes corrected-speed lines reaching 160,000 rpm, efficiency contours and corrected flow. A highest plotted speed line is not automatically a rotor mechanical limit, and the scan does not publish a 993 stock operating envelope.

questions.prompt: Does the 160,000 rpm line certify the 993 speed limit?
questions.answer: No. It is a plotted corrected-speed line for the scanned map. It does not certify the mechanical maximum or establish exact 993 applicability.

passages.text: Turbomap lists numerical compressor and turbine data for a Porsche 996 M96/70 K16-2467G application. The listed data are offered on quotation and were not acquired in this research. Complete turbo identity and correspondence with the 993 M64/60 would need verification.

questions.prompt: Does this research contain downloadable exact 993 data from Turbomap?
questions.answer: No. It establishes an offered 996 dataset, not acquired numerical data or exact 993 equivalence.

passages.text: Garrett lists a 48 mm compressor inducer, 60 mm compressor exducer, 54 mm turbine inducer and 49 mm turbine exducer for G25-550. It also publishes compressor and turbine-flow curves for this turbo family. These data describe Garrett hardware, not a K16 hybrid with a similar wheel diameter.

questions.prompt: May a 48 mm K16 hybrid use the G25-550 map by diameter alone?
questions.answer: No. A matching diameter does not establish wheel profile, clearances, diffuser, volute or turbine equivalence. The map belongs to the tested Garrett configuration.

passages.text: Garrett explicitly declares a maximum shaft speed of 185,000 rpm for G25-550. This is different evidence from merely reading the largest speed line on an unrelated map. The declaration does not apply to the Porsche K16 rotor.

questions.prompt: Which rotor has the documented 185,000 rpm limit?
questions.answer: Garrett G25-550. Do not transfer that limit to a stock K16 or a rebuilt hybrid without its own manufacturer operating limit.

passages.text: The G25-550 advertised 300-550 hp range is a single-turbo potential crank-power estimate associated with compressor choke flow. It is not a measured Porsche result or guaranteed output for a particular engine.

questions.prompt: Does the 550 hp name guarantee a 993 engine result?
questions.answer: No. It is a turbo capacity estimate under the manufacturer’s stated basis. Engine output depends on the full system and operating conditions.

passages.text: Garrett publishes compressor and turbine-flow curves for GT2860RS. Its table gives a rounded 47 mm compressor inducer and a 60 mm compressor exducer. A 60 mm compressor description should not be read as a 60 mm inducer.

questions.prompt: Which diameter describes the GT2860RS compressor inlet in this record?
questions.answer: The table’s rounded 47 mm inducer. The 60 mm dimension is the exducer, and neither dimension alone makes this a K16 map.

passages.text: BorgWarner publishes an EFR6258 compressor map with a 49 mm inducer and 62 mm outer compressor diameter. The inspected map includes a 168,000 rpm line. The complete EFR uses different hardware from a 993 K16.

questions.prompt: Is 168,000 rpm a verified K16 maximum?
questions.answer: No. It is an observed EFR6258 map line. The EFR map and construction do not establish any K16 mechanical limit.

passages.text: BorgWarner publishes an EFR6758 compressor map with a 54 mm inducer and 67 mm outer compressor diameter. The inspected map includes a 154,000 rpm line. This larger compressor comparison does not establish that a K16 housing accepts the wheel or provides the same map.

questions.prompt: Does the EFR6758 map establish the output of a K16 with a 54 mm wheel?
questions.answer: No. Wheel size alone does not identify a complete compressor. Housing geometry, clearances, wheel design and turbine matching remain different.

passages.text: The SJM Audi K24 map is associated with compressor 2470GGA/6.13 and KKK 53249707000. The family name K24 alone does not establish identity with the Porsche 993 K24 application.

questions.prompt: Can an Audi K24 map be assigned to every Porsche K24?
questions.answer: No. Verify the complete reference, compressor, turbine and housings before considering equivalence.

passages.text: SJM lists the Audi RS2 turbo as KKK 53249707200 with compressor 2672GGC for the ADU five-cylinder engine. Porsche’s historical involvement with RS2 does not make this a 993 Turbo map.

questions.prompt: Does the Porsche association make the RS2 map valid for M64/60?
questions.answer: No. The engine and turbo references differ. The historical association is not component or aerodynamic equivalence.

passages.text: A compressor map relates pressure ratio and corrected mass flow with efficiency contours and corrected shaft-speed lines. Turbine data relate expansion ratio, corrected exhaust flow and, when available, efficiency and speed. A dyno curve relates engine power or torque to engine rpm. ECU maps instead store control targets and calibration values. These are distinct data types.

questions.prompt: Which map is needed to evaluate surge and compressor efficiency?
questions.answer: The compressor map for the exact wheel and housing, using its defined corrected-flow and speed conventions. A dyno curve or ECU calibration is not a substitute.

questions.prompt: Can a dyno curve alone reveal a complete turbo map?
questions.answer: No. Engine output alone leaves inlet/outlet conditions, corrected flow, turbo speed and component efficiencies underdetermined.

passages.text: Compressor pressure ratio uses absolute outlet pressure divided by absolute inlet pressure. For an illustrative manifold pressure of 2.4 bar absolute, 0.1 bar outlet-path loss and 0.95 bar compressor-inlet pressure, the ratio is (2.4+0.1)/0.95, approximately 2.63. These pressures are scenario inputs, not measured Porsche data.

questions.prompt: What pressure ratio should be plotted for this scenario?
questions.answer: Approximately 2.63, using the compressor outlet and inlet absolute pressures. Do not divide gauge boost by ambient pressure or omit the stated losses.

passages.text: For symmetric parallel twin turbos, each compressor is sized using half the engine’s total air mass flow under the equal-flow assumption. The two compressors each develop the required pressure ratio; their pressure ratios are not added or divided by two.

questions.prompt: Should I divide both flow and pressure ratio by two?
questions.answer: Divide total flow by two only under the symmetric equal-flow assumption. Each turbo must still provide the required pressure ratio.

passages.text: Corrected-flow and corrected-speed values depend on the map’s pressure and temperature reference convention. In a common convention, m_corrected=m*sqrt(Tin/Tref)/(Pin/Pref), and N_corrected=N/sqrt(Tin/Tref). Use absolute pressure and temperature and the actual map references. A stated corrected speed is not automatically the physical shaft speed.

questions.prompt: Can corrected-speed lines be compared directly across maps with different reference conditions?
questions.answer: No. First identify each map’s reference conditions and definitions, then convert the measurements consistently. Physical shaft speed and corrected speed can differ.

passages.text: For an illustrative four-stroke engine, total air flow can be estimated as Vd*n/120*VE*pman/(R*Tman). With Vd=0.0036 m3, n=6000 rpm, VE=0.90, pman=240000 Pa, Tman=323.15 K and R=287.05 J/(kg K), equal sharing gives approximately 0.2096 kg/s per turbo. These are assumed inputs; the result is not a measured M64/60 flow or a predicted horsepower.

questions.prompt: What does the computed 0.2096 kg/s per turbo establish?
questions.answer: Only the flow requirement of the stated illustrative model. It does not establish actual engine VE, turbo efficiency, available boost, horsepower or a stock compressor map.

passages.text: Singer’s 2022 Classic Turbo description uses a Type 964-based 3.8 litre engine, electric wastegates and air/water charge cooling. It advertises 450 or 510 HP. The consulted release provides no compressor/turbine map and does not describe a stock 3.6 litre M64/60 K16 configuration.

questions.prompt: Can these Singer figures train a stock M64/60 specification?
questions.answer: They belong to the separately labeled Singer configuration. Different displacement, cooling and turbo control prevent treating them as stock M64/60 evidence.

passages.text: The 2023 DLS Turbo release describes a Type 964-based 3.8 litre four-valve engine above 700 HP and 9000 rpm. The 2026 Sorcerer description explicitly includes water-cooled heads and variable-geometry turbos, with 710 HP SAE Net. Keep the dated configurations separate; neither consulted release publishes maps for the stock 993 K16.

questions.prompt: Should the two Singer releases be merged into a single stock 993 engine record?
questions.answer: No. Preserve the release dates and configuration differences, and keep both apart from the stock M64/60. They do not establish K16 map data.

passages.application: Gunther Werks current 4.0 litre Turbo program
passages.text: The consulted Gunther Werks Turbo page describes a 993-based vehicle with a 4.0 litre twin-turbo engine, horizontal fan, Motec management and an advertised 850 bhp. It does not identify the exact turbo or publish compressor/turbine maps. A 993 body does not establish stock M64/60 internals.

questions.prompt: Does this vehicle’s 993 base establish an 850 bhp stock-engine capability?
questions.answer: No. The advertised figure belongs to a modified 4.0 litre configuration, and the turbo identity and operating maps remain unpublished in the consulted page.

passages.text: TurboMaster lists the stock 993 pair as K16-2467GGA/8.88 and displays an A/R value of 8.00. The convention behind this number was not established. Size-8 and size-10 KKK housing labels must not be treated automatically as conventional dimensionless Garrett A/R values.

questions.prompt: May I set a simulation A/R to 8.0 or 0.8 using this listing?
questions.answer: No. The vendor or KKK convention and the actual housing geometry must be confirmed before assigning a conventional A/R value.

passages.text: Within each turbo, its compressor and turbine are joined by one shaft and therefore share physical rotational speed. The two turbos are not mechanically synchronized with each other or the crankshaft. Their exact operating speeds were not established by the consulted nomenclature.

questions.prompt: At 6000 engine rpm, can I compute K16 speed from a fixed gear ratio?
questions.answer: No. The turbo shaft speed depends on gas flow, pressure ratios, temperatures and losses. No fixed engine-to-turbo ratio or exact K16 operating speed is established here.
